heroHeadline: Baidu AI Chip Unit Kunlunxin Eyes $14.6B Dual IPO (HKEX + STAR Market); MIIT Launches National AI Ethics Review Pilot Four Days Before Trump-Xi Beijing Summit
heroSubtitle: Bloomberg and South China Morning Post confirmed on May 8–10 that Kunlunxin (昆仑芯科技), Baidu's AI chip subsidiary, is pursuing a dual listing targeting HK$100 billion (~US$14.6 billion) on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and a parallel Shanghai STAR Market listing — making it the latest Chinese AI hardware company to enter public capital markets after Zhipu AI and MiniMax's January 2026 Hong Kong IPOs. Kunlunxin designs the Kunlun I and II AI accelerator chips that power Baidu's ERNIE Bot inference, Apollo autonomous driving, and enterprise Baidu AI Cloud workloads — a full-stack domestic AI silicon layer built entirely without Nvidia components. The dual IPO adds Kunlunxin to a China AI chip/model valuation constellation now exceeding $110B collectively: DeepSeek ($45B, China Big Fund-led, May 7), MiniMax ($40B+, global #4 AI model market share), Zhipu AI (~$14B, HKEX-listed), and Huawei's AI chip revenues ($12B 2026 forecast, ~60% domestic market share). This $110B+ in AI-hardware-and-model enterprise value was largely non-existent in October 2022 when the first US chip export controls were imposed — a data point that validates the export controls paradox as empirically settled: restrictions accelerated the creation of a self-capitalizing domestic AI chip ecosystem. Separately, MIIT issued a formal notice on May 10 launching a national AI ethics review pilot program in provincial AI innovation zones — establishing ethics committees, drafting review rules, and addressing algorithmic discrimination and emotional dependence risks in AI applications. The ethics pilot is the latest layer of China's AI governance architecture (following the August 2023 Generative AI Interim Measures) and arrives four days before the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14–15), where formal US-China AI dialogue on military AI safety and autonomous weapons risk is under consideration (Benzinga/CNBC, May 8). ByteDance raised its 2026 AI capex to $29.4B (May 9) with larger share going to domestic Huawei chips; Hang Seng Tech Index to gain $1.25–1.75B passive inflows when Zhipu AI and MiniMax join June 8 (Morgan Stanley, May 3); SMIC Q1 2026 results due May 14. China's AI stack — compute (Huawei Ascend), models (DeepSeek V4, Doubao, ERNIE), applications (7M vehicles, 120T tokens/day), and now capital formation ($110B+ AI chip/model IPO wave) — continues accelerating simultaneously across every layer as the Trump-Xi summit approaches.
